title: Inventory Metrics & Calculations
description: Formulas and definitions for numeric demand and inventory planning metrics displayed across the platform.

forecast.title: 14-Day Forecast
forecast.summary: Projected sales units for this item across the next 14 calendar days.
forecast.calculation: Sum of daily predicted sales for next 14 days
forecast.details: Generated by the AI demand model using sales history, trends, and seasonal patterns.
forecast.action: Drives daily sales rate (14d Forecast / 14) used to calculate Days of Supply and Reorder Point.

stock.title: On-Hand Stock
stock.summary: Available physical units currently in stock ready to fulfill orders.
stock.details: Represents immediate sellable inventory compared against Reorder Point and Safety Stock.
stock.action: Triggers status alerts when stock drops below reorder or safety buffers.

daysOfSupply.title: Days of Supply (DOS)
daysOfSupply.summary: Estimated number of days current inventory will last based on forecasted sales run-rate.
daysOfSupply.calculation: Current Stock / Daily Sales (Daily Sales = 14d Forecast / 14)
daysOfSupply.details: Measures inventory runway. When Days of Supply > 365 days, inventory is flagged as Deadstock.
daysOfSupply.action: Liquidate, discount, or halt replenishment when Days of Supply exceeds target thresholds.

reorderPoint.title: Reorder Point (ROP)
reorderPoint.summary: Inventory level threshold that signals when to place a replenishment order.
reorderPoint.calculation: (Lead Time Days * Daily Sales) + Safety Stock
reorderPoint.details: Covers expected customer demand while waiting for supplier delivery, keeping safety stock intact.
reorderPoint.action: Place purchase order when Current Stock <= Reorder Point.

safetyStock.title: Safety Stock
safetyStock.summary: Minimum reserve buffer held to protect against sudden sales spikes and vendor delays.
safetyStock.details: Insurance buffer that prevents stockouts if a supplier delivers late or demand suddenly surges.
safetyStock.action: Emergency replenish when Current Stock <= Safety Stock.

breakdown.title: Forecast Value Drivers (Breakdown)
breakdown.summary: Relative percentage share of forecast impact contributed by each feature group.
breakdown.details: Groups model features into categories (Historical Sales, Pricing, Calendar, Promotions) to explain overall 14-day demand.
breakdown.action: Identify the primary driver moving demand to guide inventory and promotion planning.

shap_mirror.title: Daily Drivers (Tree SHAP Attribution)
shap_mirror.summary: Shows exactly how many extra or fewer units customers will buy today compared to a normal day.
shap_mirror.calculation: Today's Forecast = Baseline Sales + Green Drivers (Sales Boosts) - Red Drivers (Sales Drops)
shap_mirror.details: TreeSHAP works like a fair referee dividing credit. If today's forecast is higher than usual, it shows whether the boost came from a discount, a weekend shopping wave, or great sales yesterday.
shap_mirror.action: Click any driver card to ask the assistant why that specific reason boosted or lowered sales.

shap_base_value.title: Normal Baseline Demand
shap_base_value.summary: The typical starting sales number for a product before factoring in today's specific weather, discounts, or day of the week.
shap_base_value.calculation: Starting benchmark for all daily AI calculations
shap_base_value.details: Think of this as the starting line. All green reasons add extra units to this baseline, and all red reasons subtract units from it to reach the final forecast.
shap_base_value.action: Check if today's overall conditions are giving you a net positive sales boost or dragging sales down.

sales_lag_1.title: Yesterday's Sales (sales_1)
sales_lag_1.summary: How many units sold yesterday, showing whether the product has hot customer demand right now.
sales_lag_1.details: If shoppers bought a lot yesterday, customer interest is high and today gets a positive green boost. If sales were zero yesterday, today's forecast is pulled down.
sales_lag_1.action: If yesterday had a negative pull, check if the store ran out of stock or if customer demand suddenly cooled.

sales_lag_7.title: Same Day Last Week (sales_7)
sales_lag_7.summary: How many units sold exactly 7 days ago on the same day of the week.
sales_lag_7.details: Shoppers follow weekly habits. If people buy lots of fresh bread every Saturday, last Saturday's high sales will boost the forecast for this coming Saturday.
sales_lag_7.action: Order extra stock before days that saw big sales this time last week.

sales_lag_14.title: Two Weeks Ago (sales_14)
sales_lag_14.summary: How many units sold 14 days ago, confirming whether customer buying habits are steady.
sales_lag_14.details: Checks if regular sales from two weeks ago match last week, making sure one odd day does not trick the AI forecast.
sales_lag_14.action: Confirms steady long-term buying habits across bi-weekly reorder schedules.

sales_order_interaction.title: Basket Share (sales_order_lag)
sales_order_interaction.summary: How popular this item is compared to the total number of orders placed across the whole warehouse.
sales_order_interaction.calculation: Recent item sales combined with total store orders
sales_order_interaction.details: Shows whether customers are going out of their way to buy this specific item, or if sales only went up because the whole store was busier.
sales_order_interaction.action: Stock more units if this item is becoming a must-have in almost every customer's basket.

sales_price_interaction.title: Revenue Momentum (sales_price_lag)
sales_price_interaction.summary: The total money customers recently spent on this item (quantity sold times price).
sales_price_interaction.calculation: Recent sales units multiplied by item selling price
sales_price_interaction.details: Tells the AI whether customers are still happily spending their money on this item, or if the price tag is starting to push them away.
sales_price_interaction.action: If high price is dragging down sales, consider a promotion to bring back customer volume.

sales_summary_stats.title: Average, Lowest & Peak Sales
sales_summary_stats.summary: The typical daily average, worst-day sales, and best-day sales over recent weeks.
sales_summary_stats.calculation: Average, minimum, and peak sales over the past few weeks
sales_summary_stats.details: Gives the AI a clear picture of what a standard day looks like, as well as the highest rush peak and the quietest sales floor.
sales_summary_stats.action: Use the lowest past sales number to set your emergency backup safety stock.

max_discount.title: Biggest Active Discount (max_discount)
max_discount.summary: The largest price cut currently running on this product across all promotion deals.
max_discount.details: Big discounts (like 20% to 50% off) make shoppers eager to buy, creating a strong green boost in expected sales volume.
max_discount.action: Stack extra inventory in the warehouse before big discount days to avoid selling out.

discounted_price.title: Final Checkout Price (discounted_price)
discounted_price.summary: The actual price customers pay at checkout after all active discounts are taken off.
discounted_price.calculation: Regular shelf price minus active discount
discounted_price.details: Lower checkout prices make products attractive to more people, driving up demand. High prices give a red pull that lowers expected sales.
discounted_price.action: Test different discount prices to find the sweet spot where you sell plenty of units while keeping healthy profits.

discount_lags.title: Post-Sale Slump (Discount Hangover)
discount_lags.summary: The quiet sales lull that often happens right after a big discount promotion ends.
discount_lags.calculation: Effect of discount campaigns from previous days
discount_lags.details: When shoppers stock up on a product during a big sale, they do not need to buy again for a while. This creates a temporary red dip in sales after the deal finishes.
discount_lags.action: Do not panic and over-order right after a sale ends; wait for customer stockpiles to clear.

weekday.title: Day of Week (Weekend Surge)
weekday.summary: How the natural day of the week (Monday through Sunday) changes customer shopping behavior.
weekday.calculation: Calendar day of the week effect (Monday to Sunday)
weekday.details: Families buy significantly more groceries on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday (green boost), and much less on quiet Tuesday afternoons (red drop).
weekday.action: Schedule warehouse truck deliveries to arrive a day before the busy weekend rush.

sin_cos_dayofyear.title: Time of Year (Annual Seasonality)
sin_cos_dayofyear.summary: Natural seasonal demand shifts across spring, summer, autumn, and winter holidays.
sin_cos_dayofyear.details: Helps the AI remember that cold drinks and watermelon sell best in summer, while hearty soups and holiday baking items peak in winter.
sin_cos_dayofyear.action: Order seasonal inventory well before holidays and taper off orders before the season ends.

total_orders.title: Total Warehouse Orders (total_orders)
total_orders.summary: How busy the entire warehouse is with customer orders overall.
total_orders.calculation: Total customer orders across the entire fulfillment center
total_orders.details: When bad weather or holidays cause everyone to order groceries at once, almost every product gets an extra green sales boost from store-wide traffic.
total_orders.action: Keep extra buffer stock ready whenever warehouse-wide order volume is projected to spike.

status_overview.title: Inventory Status Logic
status_overview.summary: Step-by-step check to assign each SKU an inventory health status.
status_overview.calculation: Check in order: Deadstock -> Critical -> Reorder -> Monitor -> In Stock
status_overview.details: Evaluates current stock against Reorder Point, Safety Stock, and sales velocity.
status_overview.action: Guides purchasing, expedite, and clearance decisions.
